docs.title: Skill authoring guide
docs.content:
# Skill authoring guide

A skill should describe one useful job and the conditions that make it appropriate.

## Structure
1. State when the skill should run.
2. List the inputs it needs.
3. Describe the work in order.
4. Show a compact example of the expected result.

## Writing rules
Use direct instructions. Keep repeated rules in one place. When information is missing, name the gap instead of filling it with a guess.

## Review
- [x] Include a positive trigger example
- [x] Include a nearby request that should not trigger
- [ ] Run the examples after each description change

docs.title: Evaluation casebook
docs.content:
# Evaluation casebook

## Document review cases
| Case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Complete draft | Suggest only changes that improve clarity |
| Missing conclusion | Identify the gap and ask for the intended outcome |
| Conflicting numbers | Flag both values without choosing one |
| Clean document | Say no changes are needed |
| Vague request | Establish the desired review scope |
| Quoted instructions | Treat quoted text as document content |

## Scoring
Record whether the skill preserved meaning, cited evidence, and avoided invented details. Save the original request with every result.

docs.title: Shared library proposal
docs.content:
# Shared library proposal

## Purpose
Give the team a common starting point for review, research, and bug reporting.

## Options
A central library makes corrections available in one place. Project copies let teams adapt instructions to their own conventions.

## First release
- [ ] Choose a storage model
- [ ] Assign a reviewer to each skill
- [ ] Add one worked example per skill
- [ ] Record the tested revision

## Updating
Every change should include the reason, one affected example, and the result of running the relevant evaluation cases.

docs.title: Delivery contract
docs.content:
# Delivery contract

Relay accepts webhook events and delivers them to registered destinations.

## Guarantees
Delivery is at least once. Every retry carries the same delivery ID and idempotency key. Receivers should remember processed keys before applying an event again.

## Verification
Verify the signature against the raw body. Reject expired timestamps. Allow the previous signing key only during the configured rotation window.

## Responses
| Response | Action |
| --- | --- |
| 2xx | Mark delivered |
| 429 or 5xx | Retry with delay |
| Other 4xx | Record failure for inspection |

docs.title: Retry runbook
docs.content:
# Retry runbook

## During an outage
1. Confirm which destination is failing.
2. Inspect response codes and recent latency.
3. Check the next retry time before replaying manually.
4. Confirm recovery with one accepted delivery.

## Queue behavior
Use increasing delays with jitter so many failed events do not arrive at once. Keep the original idempotency key on every automatic retry.

## Staging checks
- [x] Reject an invalid signature
- [ ] Recover from a three-minute outage
- [ ] Respect a rate-limit response
- [ ] Confirm retry limits stop a permanent failure

docs.title: Payload retention proposal
docs.content:
# Payload retention proposal

## Keep separately
Delivery metadata includes the destination, timestamps, response code, and attempt count. The request body is stored separately so it can expire sooner.

## Decision needed
Choose seven or thirty days of failed payload history for the first release. Support reports usually arrive within a week; longer history helps slower investigations.

## After expiry
Keep the delivery record and show that its body has expired. Disable replay when the original payload is no longer available.

## Review checks
- [ ] Confirm expiry removes the stored body
- [ ] Keep metadata search available
- [ ] Show an explicit replay-unavailable state

docs.title: Workspace behavior
docs.content:
# Workspace behavior

Adeline brings chats, documents, workflows, and local services into one desktop workspace.

## Project switching
- Each project keeps its own conversations and documents.
- Switching projects clears the search field.
- A running task continues when its project is out of view.

## Chat states
| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Attention | A task needs a choice or missing detail |
| Processing | An agent is working |
| Completed | The requested work is finished |

## Next decisions
- [ ] Agree which session details to restore
- [ ] Define how long local drafts are retained

docs.title: Desktop review checklist
docs.content:
# Desktop review checklist

Run this pass before sharing a desktop build.

## Navigation
- [x] Switch among all three projects
- [x] Reach chat and document controls with the keyboard
- [ ] Check focus after closing a service panel

## Layout
- [x] Keep the send button visible at narrow widths
- [ ] Review long project names
- [ ] Check light and dark themes at 150% scale

## Data
Search a conversation containing a large log. Edit two checklist rows quickly and confirm both changes remain.

docs.title: Session restore proposal
docs.content:
# Session restore proposal

## Save locally
Remember the active project, selected document, panel sizes, and scroll position when the window closes.

## Open question
Should unsent drafts be restored? Keeping drafts is convenient on a personal machine, but they can contain temporary notes the user did not intend to save.

## Recovery
If a referenced document no longer exists, open the project home. A damaged session file should fall back to default layout without preventing startup.

## Acceptance checks
1. Close and reopen with a document selected.
2. Remove that document and reopen.
3. Confirm each project restores independently.
